title: Answer Across a Deterministic Run
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine, let $\beta$ be a Boolean value, and suppose the deterministic machine that follows $A$'s deterministic instructions and replaces each choice instruction by an immediate return of $\beta$ takes $T$ steps from configuration $a$ to configuration $a'$. Assume that at every time $t<T$, whenever this run is still active, the instruction of $A$ at its current state is deterministic. For any natural number $N$ and Boolean value $b$, a choice sequence of length $T+N$ leaving answer $b$ from $a$ exists if and only if a choice sequence of length $N$ leaving answer $b$ from $a'$ exists.
hypotheses_covered: machine A and Boolean value β
configurations a and a′ and natural number T
the deterministic run of length T from a ends at a′
